title: Ombudsman prosecutor: No document shows Romualdez directed Co on budget matters
summary: A prosecution witness said Tuesday there were no documents showing former House speaker and Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez directed former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of…

blocks.text: A prosecution witness said Tuesday there were no documents showing former House speaker and Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez directed former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list on budget matters.

Assistant Special Prosecutor Joshua Tan of the Office of the Ombudsman made the testimony during the bail hearing of Romualdez, who is facing a P7.4-billion plunder case alongside Co and others over their alleged links to the flood control kickback scheme.

During the cross examination of Romualdez's counsel Rashel Pomoy, Tan was asked if there were documents showing that Romualdez provided instructions to Co on budget allocations. It has been the prosecution's theory that Romualdez was the central figure in the budget for flood control projects, and that it was Co who identified projects and made insertions in the proposed budget.

Asked by Pomoy if the prosecution's argument of Romualdez giving instructions to Co was based on inference, Tan replied, "Yes," but qualified it by saying it was "based on the evidence gathered by the Special Panel of Investigators."

Pomoy also asked Tan if Ombudsman investigators found documents from a contractor, Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) personnel, or any other contract showing that Romualdez received commission from any of them, Tan replied: "None."
Tan also confirmed that state witness Roberto Bernardo, a former Public Works undersecretary, only testified that he only dealt with Co, not Romualdez.
During the redirect examination by Deputy Special Prosecutor Omar Sagadal, Tan said, "central figures are never the front."
“You [as a central figure] will never be at the front yourself. Otherwise, it would be pointless,” Tan said.
Tan said there were also three sets of independent evidence showing that pieces of luggage containing money were delivered to property registered under Romualdez.
"If that [delivery] is true, what would be the reason for that," Tan said.

According to Tan, the Ombudsman was still investigating Romualdez and apparent associate Jose Paras for a separate money laundering offense due to the latter's purchase of two properties in Forbes Park, which the prosecution argues are way above the financial capacity of Paras.
The prosecution alleges that the companies used by Paras to buy the properties are linked to Romualdez, making the former House speaker the real buyer.
Tan, however, said Romualdez is not a stockholder in the Golden Pheasant and Brightnews firms used by Paras to make such purchases. — VDV, GMA News
